transcript.text: Alright everyone, before I can give final approval on the shoot plan for tonight at Riverside Foundry, I need status checks from each of your departments. We've got a free-flying drone shot, six hours of horse work, a pyrotechnic spark wall, and an 11:00 PM wrap on the board. Street parking is reserved from 6:00 PM to 11:00 PM. Let's hear from cinematography, animal coordination, special effects, and location management — what's your status?

transcript.text: Before I give my cinematography status, I need to flag a permit issue. I confirmed with the aviation-permit vendor this afternoon that the Riverside Foundry permit allows only a tethered drone, not a free-flying drone, and requires a licensed drone operator to be listed on the plan. The vendor's confirmation is still in the cinematography equipment file. The current draft plan calls for a free-flying drone shot, which would violate the permit.
transcript.speaker: A2

transcript.text: I need to flag an animal welfare issue. My animal-welfare representative confirmed today that the horse may work for no more than 4 hours total, and must receive a 30-minute rest break after each 2-hour work block. I haven't yet added this confirmation to the animal-use worksheet. The current draft plan calls for six hours of horse work, which would exceed the 4-hour limit. This needs to be revised before I can give a clean animal coordination status.
transcript.speaker: A3

transcript.text: I need to flag an insurance issue for my special effects status. I confirmed with the production insurer that pyrotechnic effects are excluded from this shoot's policy, while atmospheric haze is covered. The insurer requires that any effect substitution be recorded in the effects plan. The current draft plan calls for a pyrotechnic spark wall, which would not be covered under our policy. We'll need to substitute atmospheric haze for the spark wall and document the substitution in the effects plan before I can give a clean status.
transcript.speaker: A4

transcript.text: I need to flag a location permit issue for my location management status. I received the signed neighborhood filming permit this morning, which requires production to wrap by exactly 10:00 PM — not 11:00 PM as the draft plan states — and the street-parking closure is only valid from 6:00 PM through 10:00 PM, not until 11:00 PM. I have not yet replaced the draft location sheet, so the current draft still reflects the old 11:00 PM wrap and 6:00 PM–11:00 PM parking window. This needs to be corrected before I can give a clean location management status.
